card.name: First-person possessives in personal speech
card.fires_on: The word "my" (or a word right after it or after "I") in first-person remarks about family, patients or home, in quotes, comments and blog posts.

modes.label: "my" after a verb or preposition
modes.description: The word "my" opens a phrase about the speaker's own people or place.
modes.example: “I’ve always felt the same way, and I tell<< my>> patients the same thing.”

modes.label: Word after "my" or "I"
modes.description: The noun or verb that follows a first-person opener in a personal story.
modes.example: I just<< had>> a fun idea.

card.plain: It lights up when someone speaks about themselves and their own family, patients or home, especially at the word "my".
evidence: I’ve always felt the same way, and I tell<< my>> patients the same thing.
Unfortunately, both<< my>> husband and I have failed at our marriage
I saw a fun one at<< my>> daughter's school.
